chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: October 1945 Hodes Hot Five with Bechet and Wild Bill Davidson
summary: Welburn lists the Blue Note date; Moore recalls Davidson in uniform, his side-mouth embouchure, and the Vanguard succession.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Okay. In the following month, October 12, 1945, also for Blue Note, you recorded with Art Hodes Hot Five...

...with Pops Foster again, and Wild Bill Davidson was on cornet, and Sidney Bechet was playing clarinet and soprano. The band made six sides. There's "Save It Pretty Mama," "Way Down Yonder In New Orleans,"
"Memphis Blues," "Shine," St. James Infirmary," and "Darktown Strutters Ball." Now, had you met Wild Bill Davidson before this session? Had you ever met up with him?

Well, during that time, Wild Bill Davidson had just come in... He was in the Army. He had a uniform on. And he lived up to that name, Wild Bill, the way he... He had his own style of playing. Nobody played like him. Of course, a lot of trumpet players now are trying to imitate him, you know. He'd play on the side of his mouth; his mouthpiece was on the side of his mouth. And he was down at the Village Vanguard with us after Max Kaminsky. They had Sol Yaged down there for a while.
He was down there for a while.
